svg.title: What the USPS tracking status guide says: statuses before USPS has the package, moving through the network, out for delivery, notice left or pickup, marked delivered but not found, and when USPS says to ask for help.
svg.text: USPS tracking statuses
What USPS's guide says
Before USPS has it
Label created, shipping partner scans and
pre-shipment: the FAQ says USPS does not
have the package yet. Contact the shipper.
Moving through the network
In Transit, Arrived at and Departed USPS
Facility can repeat, on the same or on
different days. Forwarded: a change of
address or the wrong Post Office.
Out for delivery
Prepared for delivery; a carrier delivers it
today, maybe later in the day. No Delivered
scan by 9 pm local: Delivery Status Not
Updated, expected the next business day.
Notice left, pickup or hold
Signature needed, nobody home or no secure
spot: no automatic second attempt. Options:
schedule a redelivery, pick it up, or ask for
it to be returned to the sender.
Marked delivered but not found
Check the garage, household, mailbox, porch,
covered spots, doors, a parcel locker (key in
the mailbox) or the building office.
When the FAQ says to ask USPS
Out for Delivery, Arrived at Post Office, Not
Updated and Delivered: after 1 full postal
business day. No Access: after 24 hours.
Use the tracking number: service request.
Sources: two USPS FAQs (Sept. 29 and Sept. 17,
